$comment: PLACEHOLDER RECORDS — refund requests. Replaced by GET /admin/finance/refunds and POST /admin/finance/refunds/{id}/{approve,send-back,decline,pay}. A refund is a REAL OBJECT: request, queue, decision, and — once money actually moves — a settlement. Finance requests; only Super Admin decides — one of the very few genuine four-eyes checks in the panel, because a refund is the only routine action that sends money out of the company, and requester and decider are always different people. Two origins: `subscription` ties back to a recorded installment payment; `manual` is raised by hand against its own named payee, for money that never became a subscription payment in the first place — a duplicate bank transfer, a cancelled order taken off-platform, a customer overpayment. On a subscription-origin refund, `subscriptionId` is a convenience denormalisation for display only; `paymentId` is the real link back to the ledger. Approval authorises a transfer a human makes in the bank — it does not move money by itself. A refund reaches `paid` only when someone records that transfer, with its own reference, in `settlement`.

requests.detail: An NEFT of ₹22,000 arrived on 23 Aug referencing 'IB DUPLICATE PLS REFUND' — the sender says it was meant for a different vendor and landed with us by mistake. No invoice, deal or subscription in the system matches the name, the amount or the reference; the transfer never became a subscription payment, so there is no ledger row for a policy check to run against. Returning it to the account it came from.
requests.$comment: policy is null here, not an empty pass. There is no original payment on this transfer to check against, and an empty RefundPolicy would read as one that passed four checks it never ran. Manual refunds are never scored.

events.note: Manual · unmatched NEFT of ₹22,000, 23 Aug — no deal, invoice or subscription corresponds to it. Returning to sender.

requests.detail: Customer was charged twice for the same plan on 16 Aug — PAY-4399 and PAY-4400 carry the same amount and the same card token. PAY-4400 is the one to keep.

policy.$comment: Computed at request time and frozen so the approver sees what the requester saw. The check frames the approval: it does not block it. `originalRecorded` asks only whether the money is in the ledger — there is no verification step it could be waiting on.

events.note: Duplicate charge · PAY-4400 confirmed present — same amount, same token, 16 Aug.
